questions.question: Train A running at 81 km/h takes 72 sec to overtake train B, when both the trains are running in the same direction, but it takes 36 sec to cross each other if the trains are running in the opposite direction. If the length of train B is 600 metres, then find the length of train A. (in metres)
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of **Time taken** (Same direction : Opposite direction) = 72 : 36 = 2 : 1.

Ratio of **Relative Speed** (Same : Opposite) = 1 : 2 (since Distance is same).

Let speeds be VA and VB. ⇒ (VA − VB) / (VA + VB) = 1 / 2.

By Componendo and Dividendo, VA / VB = (2+1) / (2−1) = 3 / 1.

Given VA = 81 km/h ⇒ VB = 27 km/h. Total Distance (LA + LB) = Relative speed (Opposite) × Time = (81 + 27) × (5/18) × 36 = 1080 m.

LA = 1080 − 600 = 480 m.

**∴ The correct answer is 480 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/783bb2f6a08a59b0c2e0ce42af1e5088c28ec7461e131809d88fb61f7c53c3f9.png] 

**Given:** Speed of Train A (VA) = 81 km/h, Length of Train B (LB) = 600 m.

**Formula:** Distance = Relative Speed × Time; 1 km/h = 5/18 m/s.

⇒ Let LA be length of Train A and VB be speed of Train B.

⇒ Case 1 (Same direction): LA + 600 = (81 − VB) × (5/18) × 72

⇒ LA + 600 = (81 − VB) × 20 ... (i)

⇒ Case 2 (Opposite direction): LA + 600 = (81 + VB) × (5/18) × 36

⇒ LA + 600 = (81 + VB) × 10 ... (ii)

⇒ Equating (i) and (ii): (81 − VB) × 20 = (81 + VB) × 10

⇒ 162 − 2VB = 81 + VB ⇒ 3VB = 81 ⇒ VB = 27 km/h

⇒ LA + 600 = (81 + 27) × 10 = 1080

⇒ LA = 1080 − 600 = 480 m

**∴ The correct answer is 480 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed Concept

When two objects move in the **same direction**, relative speed is |V₁ − V₂|. When moving in the **opposite direction**, it is V₁ + V₂.

Crossing Distance

To fully cross or overtake each other, two trains must cover a distance equal to the **sum of their lengths** (L₁ + L₂).

Speed Conversion

To convert speed from **km/h to m/s**, multiply by 5/18. To convert from **m/s to km/h**, multiply by 18/5.</p

questions.question: Two trains P and Q start from stations S and T towards each other. Train P takes 4 hours 48 minutes and train Q takes 3 hours 20 minutes to reach T and S, respectively, after they meet. If the speed of train P is 45 km/h, what is the speed of train Q?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

After meeting, trains P and Q complete their journey in 4 hours 48 minutes and 3 hours 20 minutes respectively

Speed of train P = 45 km/hr

**Formula used:**

After meeting each other, the time required by the trains to reach the destination

(S₁)/(S₂) = sqrt{(T₂)/(T₁)} 

Where, S₁ and S₂ are the speeds of trains, and T₁ and T₂ are the times taken by trains to reach the destination after meeting

**Calculation:**

4 hours 48 minutes = 24/5 hours

3 hours 20 minutes = 10/3 hours

According to the question,

(45)/(S₂) = sqrt{((10/3))/((24/5))} 

⇒ (45)/(S₂) = sqrt{(10×5)/(24×3)} 

⇒ (45)/(S₂) = (5)/(6)

⇒ S₂ = (45 × 6)/5 = 54

**∴ The speed of Q is 54 km/hr.**

questions.question: Two trains of lengths 150 m and 250 m run on parallel lines. When they run in the same direction, they take 20 seconds to cross each other and, when they run in the opposite direction, they take 5 seconds to cross each other. What is the speed of the two trains?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total distance = 150 + 250 = 400 m.

Relative speed in same direction = S₁ − S₂ = 400 ÷ 20 = 20 m/s.

Relative speed in opposite direction = S₁ + S₂ = 400 ÷ 5 = 80 m/s.

Solving, S₁ = (80 + 20) ÷ 2 = 50 m/s and S₂ = (80 − 20) ÷ 2 = 30 m/s.

Speeds in km/h = 50 × (18/5) = 180 km/h and 30 × (18/5) = 108 km/h.

**∴ The correct answer is 180 km/h and 108 km/h.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Length of first train (L₁) = 150 m

Length of second train (L₂) = 250 m

Time taken to cross in same direction (T₁) = 20 seconds

Time taken to cross in opposite direction (T₂) = 5 seconds

**Formula Used:**

Speed = Distance ÷ Time

Total distance covered to cross each other = L₁ + L₂

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/16430e557035d55fee350ec3e082cf14d0f49e9acdc012923f1823d994f2e282.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total Distance = 150 + 250 = 400 m

⇒ Let the speed of the first train be u m/s and the second train be v m/s.

⇒ When running in the same direction, relative speed = u − v

⇒ u − v = 400 ÷ 20 = 20 m/s ... (Equation 1)

⇒ When running in opposite directions, relative speed = u + v

⇒ u + v = 400 ÷ 5 = 80 m/s ... (Equation 2)

⇒ Adding Equation 1 and Equation 2:

⇒ 2u = 100 ⇒ u = 50 m/s

⇒ Subtracting Equation 1 from Equation 2:

⇒ 2v = 60 ⇒ v = 30 m/s

⇒ Convert speeds to km/h by multiplying with (18/5):

⇒ Speed of first train = 50 × (18/5) = 180 km/h

⇒ Speed of second train = 30 × (18/5) = 108 km/h

**∴ The correct answer is 180 km/h and 108 km/h.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed

When two objects move in opposite directions, their relative speed is the sum of their individual speeds (S₁ + S₂). When moving in the same direction, it is the difference of their speeds (|S₁ − S₂|).

Distance While Crossing

When two trains cross each other, the total distance covered is always the sum of their lengths (L₁ + L₂), regardless of the direction they are moving.

Unit Conversion Trick

To rapidly convert speed from m/s to km/h, multiply the value by 18/5. To convert from km/h to m/s, multiply by 5/18.
</p

questions.question: S₁ and S₂ are two stations which are 195 km apart. A train starts from S₁ at 4:00 pm and moves towards S₂ at the speed of 65 km/h. Another train starts from S₂ at 5:00 pm and moves towards S₁ at the speed of 35 km/h. At what time will the two trains meet?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

**Relative Speed** approach: First, make the starting times the same.

In 1 hour (from 4:00 pm to 5:00 pm), **Train 1** covers 65 km.

Remaining distance at 5:00 pm = 195 − 65 = 130 km.

Relative speed (opposite direction) = 65 + 35 = 100 km/h.

Time to meet after 5:00 pm = 130 ÷ 100 = 1.3 hours = 1 hour 18 minutes.

Meeting time = 5:00 pm + 1 hour 18 minutes = 6:18 pm.

**∴ The correct answer is 6:18 p.m.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Distance = 195 km, Speed S₁ = 65 km/h (at 4 pm), Speed S₂ = 35 km/h (at 5 pm).

**Formula Used:** Time = Distance ÷ Relative Speed

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/19d7fd405248fc37c6224d7f1c1ba1950c60538d14391eff891ad4c21e33e14f.png] 

⇒ Distance covered by first train in 1 hour (4 pm to 5 pm) = 65 × 1 = 65 km.

⇒ Remaining distance = 195 − 65 = 130 km.

⇒ Relative speed = 65 + 35 = 100 km/h.

⇒ Time taken to meet = 130 ÷ 100 = 1.3 hours.

⇒ 0.3 hours = 0.3 × 60 = 18 minutes.

⇒ Meeting time = 5:00 pm + 1 hour 18 minutes = 6:18 pm.

**∴ The correct answer is 6:18 p.m.**

**__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed in Opposite Direction

When two objects move towards each other, their relative speed is the sum of their individual speeds (S₁ + S₂).

Relative Speed in Same Direction

When two objects move in the same direction, their relative speed is the difference of their individual speeds (S₁ − S₂).

Meeting Time Concept

To calculate meeting time using relative speed, ensure the distance used is the separation between the objects at the **same instant** of time.</p

Relative Speed (Same direction) = S₂ − S₁

Distance (Length of faster train) = Relative Speed × Time

**Calculations:**

⇒ Relative Speed = 48 − 36 = 12 km/hr

⇒ Conversion to m/s = 12 × (5/18) m/s

questions.question: A train traveling at 70 km/h crosses another train traveling in the same direction at 34 km/h in 25 seconds. What is the combined length of both the trains (in metres)?

Speed in m/s = 36 × (5/18) = 10 m/s.

Combined length of trains = Relative speed × Time = 10 m/s × 25 sec = 250 m.

**∴ The correct answer is 250 m.**

**Given:**

Speed of the **faster train** (S₁) = 70 km/h

Speed of the **slower train** (S₂) = 34 km/h

**Time taken** to cross (t) = 25 seconds

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/6e6f5707fcce84b8759560ec979014004ca86ac2e5dba4eb7724e6d87be1db8d.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Relative Speed = S₁ − S₂ (Same direction)

⇒ Relative Speed = 70 − 34 = 36 km/h

⇒ Speed in m/s = 36 × (5/18) = 10 m/s

⇒ Combined length = 10 × 25

⇒ Combined length = 250 m

**∴ The correct answer is 250 m.**

**__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed Concept

When two objects move in the **same direction**, relative speed = S₁ − S₂. When they move in **opposite directions**, relative speed = S₁ + S₂.

Unit Conversion

To convert speed from **km/h to m/s**, multiply by 5/18. To convert **m/s to km/h**, multiply by 18/5.

Train Crossing Total Distance

The distance covered when one train crosses another is always the **sum of the lengths** of both trains, regardless of direction.</p

questions.question: Two goods trains 132 m and 108 m in length are running towards each other on parallel tracks. The first train is running at a speed of 32 km/h and the second at a speed of 40 km/h. How much time will they take to cross each other after meeting?

**∴ The correct answer is 12 s.**

Speed in m/s = Speed in km/h × (5/18)

questions.question: A train of length 300 metres crosses a tree in 20 seconds and crosses another train of the same length travelling in opposite direction in 25 seconds. What is the speed of the second train?
